dedupe_keys.name: compute atlas us compute facilities and dedicated power inventory

description: Compute Atlas is a source-cited inventory of US data centres, cryptocurrency mining sites and power-generation facilities built to supply them. Edward Kubiak publishes facility records with operators, coordinates, planned and operational capacity, dated status changes and source references. Additional fields cover water, emissions, subsidies and other site attributes where documented. The live statistics endpoint read on 28 September 2026 reports 2,242 records, with an edition timestamp of 25 September. Its 55 jurisdiction codes include states, Washington DC and territories. Coverage is a changing project inventory, not a measured electricity-demand time series. Data are freely available through public JSON endpoints and a repository snapshot under CC BY 4.0; software uses MIT. A limitation is that disclosure varies by field and the bulk snapshot may lag the live service. Proposed capacity is not operational capacity, and permitted emissions are regulatory ceilings, not measured releases. Simulation uses include facility siting, future power-demand scenarios and dependencies between computing and generation. It complements data-atlas-global-data-center-map with a different US project-and-power scope. No facility payload or source attachment was downloaded, and individual claims were not independently re-audited.
